packageRules.description: A release is left to settle before it is proposed, so a version withdrawn within days of publication is never the one this tree is bumped to. A vulnerability fix overrides this, above.
A major is a breaking line. It waits longer, and it is labeled so it is read before merge.
Nothing is automerged. This repository has no required status check, so a merge can land before the workflow finishes.
The terminal UI is drawn by these modules together and they release in step, so proposing them separately produces a tree that has never been built as a whole.
Actions are pinned to a digest and read only by the pipeline, so a bump is verified by the run that carries it.

golangci-lint is named twice in the workflow: the action pin and the version the action runs. The github-actions manager reads the uses line and not the version beneath it, so both move in one pull request.
govulncheck decides what the vulnerability job reports, so its own update is read rather than merged unseen.
The go line is the toolchain the workflow and the release binaries compile with. A newer release is a compatibility claim, so it is raised deliberately.

customManagers.description: The golangci-lint release the workflow tells the action to run.
The govulncheck version the vulnerability job installs. It is not a module this binary imports.
